\section[\texorpdfstring{\ta{மின்கலம்} (miṉkalam)}{மின்கலம் (miṉkalam)}]{\ta{மின்கலம்} (miṉkalam) — a battery}

\label{lesson:TA-C517-minkalam}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for a video, then the Tamil for a user.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{மின்கலம்}}
\textbf{\ta{மின்கலம்}} — \emph{miṉkalam} — \textquotedblleft{}a battery\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ta{கடிகாரத்தின்} \ta{மின்கலம்} \ta{தீர்ந்துவிட்டது}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kaṭikārattiṉ miṉkalam tīrntuviṭṭatu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The clock's battery has run down.
\end{quote}

\ta{மின்} \textquotedblleft{}electric\textquotedblright{} + \ta{கலம்} \textquotedblleft{}a vessel\textquotedblright{}: a vessel of electricity.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ta{மின்கலம்}} (\emph{miṉkalam}) is a modern native compound: \ta{மின்} (\emph{miṉ}), \textquotedblleft{}lightning, electric\textquotedblright{} (DEDR 4876), and \ta{கலம்} (\emph{kalam}), \textquotedblleft{}a vessel\textquotedblright{} (DEDR 1305).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{miṉkalam}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{miṉkalam}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kaṭikārattiṉ miṉkalam tīrntuviṭṭatu.} — The clock's battery has run down.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for a video, then the Tamil for a user, then say \emph{miṉkalam} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ta{மின்கலம்} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A battery\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ta{மின்னேற்று} (miṉṉēṟṟu)}{மின்னேற்று (miṉṉēṟṟu)}]{\ta{மின்னேற்று} (miṉṉēṟṟu) — to charge (a battery)}

\label{lesson:TA-C517-minnerru}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for a user, then the Tamil for a battery.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{மின்னேற்று}}
\textbf{\ta{மின்னேற்று}} — \emph{miṉṉēṟṟu} — \textquotedblleft{}to charge (a battery)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ta{தூங்கும்} \ta{முன்} \ta{நான்} \ta{கைப்பேசியை} \ta{மின்னேற்றினேன்}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{tūṅkum muṉ nāṉ kaippēciyai miṉṉēṟṟiṉēṉ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Before sleeping I charged my phone.
\end{quote}

Past (I …): \ta{மின்னேற்றினேன்}, \emph{miṉṉēṟṟiṉēṉ}.

What is charged takes -\ta{ஐ}: \ta{கைப்பேசியை} \ta{மின்னேற்று}. In speech many people use the English word charge.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ta{மின்னேற்று}} (\emph{miṉṉēṟṟu}) is a modern native compound: \ta{மின்} (\emph{miṉ}), \textquotedblleft{}electric\textquotedblright{} (DEDR 4876), and \ta{ஏற்று} (\emph{ēṟṟu}), \textquotedblleft{}to load, to raise\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{miṉṉēṟṟu}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{miṉṉēṟṟu}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tūṅkum muṉ nāṉ kaippēciyai miṉṉēṟṟiṉēṉ.} — Before sleeping I charged my phone.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for a user, then the Tamil for a battery, then say \emph{miṉṉēṟṟu} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ta{மின்னேற்று} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To charge (a battery)\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ta{கம்பி} (kampi)}{கம்பி (kampi)}]{\ta{கம்பி} (kampi) — a wire; a metal rod}

\label{lesson:TA-C517-kampi}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for a battery, then the Tamil for to charge.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{கம்பி}}
\textbf{\ta{கம்பி}} — \emph{kampi} — \textquotedblleft{}a wire; a metal rod\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ta{அந்தக்} \ta{கம்பியில்} \ta{மின்சாரம்} \ta{இருக்கிறது}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{antak kampiyil miṉcāram irukkiṟatu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
There is electricity in that wire.
\end{quote}

It names a thin wire and a thicker iron rod alike, as in a window grille.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ta{கம்பி}} (\emph{kampi}) is native Dravidian: DEDR 1241 gives \ta{கம்பி} (\emph{kampi}) for a wire of gold, silver or iron.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kampi}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kampi}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{antak kampiyil miṉcāram irukkiṟatu.} — There is electricity in that wire.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for a battery, then the Tamil for to charge, then say \emph{kampi} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ta{கம்பி} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A wire; a metal rod\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ta{துண்டி} (tuṇṭi)}{துண்டி (tuṇṭi)}]{\ta{துண்டி} (tuṇṭi) — to disconnect; to cut off}

\label{lesson:TA-C517-tunti}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for to charge, then the Tamil for a wire.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{துண்டி}}
\textbf{\ta{துண்டி}} — \emph{tuṇṭi} — \textquotedblleft{}to disconnect; to cut off\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ta{புயலால்} \ta{எங்கள்} \ta{ஊரின்} \ta{மின்சாரம்} \ta{துண்டிக்கப்பட்டது}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{puyalāl eṅkaḷ ūriṉ miṉcāram tuṇṭikkappaṭṭatu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Because of the storm our town's electricity was cut off.
\end{quote}

Past (I …): \ta{துண்டித்தேன்}, \emph{tuṇṭittēṉ}.

The passive ending -\ta{ப்படு} makes \textquotedblleft{}was cut off\textquotedblright{}: \ta{துண்டிக்கப்பட்டது}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ta{துண்டி}} (\emph{tuṇṭi}) is native Dravidian: DEDR 3310 gives \ta{துண்டு} (\emph{tuṇṭu}), \textquotedblleft{}a piece, a fragment\textquotedblright{}, and the verb \ta{துண்டி} (\emph{tuṇṭi}), \textquotedblleft{}to cut, to sever, to divide\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tuṇṭi}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tuṇṭi}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{puyalāl eṅkaḷ ūriṉ miṉcāram tuṇṭikkappaṭṭatu.} — Because of the storm our town's electricity was cut off.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for to charge, then the Tamil for a wire, then say \emph{tuṇṭi} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ta{துண்டி} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To disconnect; to cut off\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ta{ஒளிர்} (oḷir)}{ஒளிர் (oḷir)}]{\ta{ஒளிர்} (oḷir) — to glow; to shine}

\label{lesson:TA-C517-olir}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for a wire, then the Tamil for to disconnect.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{ஒளிர்}}
\textbf{\ta{ஒளிர்}} — \emph{oḷir} — \textquotedblleft{}to glow; to shine\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ta{இருட்டில்} \ta{கடிகாரத்தின்} \ta{எண்கள்} \ta{ஒளிர்கின்றன}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{iruṭṭil kaṭikārattiṉ eṇkaḷ oḷirkiṉṟaṉa.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
In the dark the clock's numbers glow.
\end{quote}

Past (it …): \ta{ஒளிர்ந்தது}, \emph{oḷirntatu}.

The subject is usually a light or a thing that shines, so the past is shown with \ta{அது}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ta{ஒளிர்}} (\emph{oḷir}) is native Dravidian: DEDR 1016 gives \ta{ஒளி} (\emph{oḷi}), \textquotedblleft{}light, brightness\textquotedblright{}, and the verb \ta{ஒளிர்} (\emph{oḷir}), \textquotedblleft{}to shine\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{oḷir}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{oḷir}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{iruṭṭil kaṭikārattiṉ eṇkaḷ oḷirkiṉṟaṉa.} — In the dark the clock's numbers glow.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for a wire, then the Tamil for to disconnect, then say \emph{oḷir} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ta{ஒளிர்} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To glow; to shine\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
